chapter: California, Art Tatum and Lionel Hampton
title: Thrill of playing with Hamp; leaving after Chicago's Grand Terrace
summary: He was nervous and thrilled to play with Hampton, but left after Chicago's Grand Terrace over too little playing, pneumonia and band business.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: What did you feel about Hamp?
What did I feel about Hamp?

To me it was the greatest thrill I ever had in my life, because I just -- I thought Lionel Hampton was one of the most talented musicians I'd ever seen in my life, and I was just flabbergasted to play with. In fact I was so nervous that I couldn't play, hardly, because -- of course, you know, Lionel used to like play both ends of the piano and you never knew which end he was going to get on.

And then he did so many things, I mean there was so much going on. Actually, I just considered myself very lucky to be with so many fine musicians, and I really just enjoyed every minute of it. You know.

And we later on went to Chicago and played in the Grand Terrace for a while, and that's where I decided --I thought I wanted to go on my own, because I didn't get a chance to play enough in the big band, and there were several things I didn't like about the business of the band. And I got sick also, I had a little summer pneumonia there and I just wasn't too happy.
And I decided to go on to New York on my own, I went to Buffalo, New York first and then I finally went on to New York.
